official.application_cycle: Selection takes place once a year although applications can be submitted at any time; fully completed applications must be registered in the EMBO application portal by 23:59 CEST on 30 October of each year.
official.status_note: The official programme pages display 'Apply by 30 October' with an active application link; applications are accepted continuously, only fully completed applications are considered, and applicants are notified of the outcome by email by mid-November.
benefits: Daily stipend based on the cost of living in the country of the placement/s
The stipends are intended to cover living expenses and travel costs

Daily rate in Euro per country of placement, published by EMBO at EUR 68-140 per day (CHF-level Switzerland EUR 140, Ireland/United Kingdom EUR 100, Germany/France/Netherlands/Austria/Belgium EUR 93, most central and eastern European states EUR 68), plus a travel allowance of EUR 350 for most countries (EUR 800 Chile, Singapore, Taiwan; EUR 600 India; EUR 500 Israel)
Journalist Fellows will also be expected to attend a two-day workshop at EMBO in Heidelberg, Germany for which travel and accommodation will be provided
This scheme was made possible by a private donation from Professor Maria Leptin
eligibility: Applicants must reside in an EMBC Member State, and their placement/s must also occur in an EMBC Member State
The placements must be in-person; virtual placements are not eligible
If Fellows wish to undertake two or more placements at least one must be in a different EMBC Member State than the other/s; applicants are not subject to any age restriction

Journalists must be able to demonstrate relevant experience of working as an employed or freelance journalist as their main occupation and provide appropriate samples of their published or broadcast work

Life scientists seeking support to transition into full time (science) journalism must have a master's degree or higher, and preferably in a life sciences discipline, and must demonstrate a genuine desire to transition into journalism as a profession, including suitable evidence of prior reporting on the life sciences and/or associated disciplines
Personal blog posts or social media postings, or publication in academic journals of commentary or reviews of research, are not considered sufficient evidence of prior journalism

Fellows are expected to not undertake other work during the term of their fellowship; Journalists must not report on their host research institution during the term of their fellowship; it is not possible to extend the scholarship period
requirements: Proposal in English of a maximum of three pages explaining how the fellowship will be used to broaden and deepen knowledge of research, the research process and/or relevant technologies in the life sciences and associated disciplines (researchers: demonstrating a genuine desire to transition from research to journalism and how the fellowship would improve their knowledge and practice of journalism)

Proposal must specify the nominated research institution/s and expected specific learning and knowledge outcomes (researchers: a newsroom/s for a full-time internship or similar in a mainstream media newsroom, producing published or broadcast science journalism)
Proposal should be discussed with the proposed host institution/newsroom prior to submitting; formal written confirmation of acceptance is not required at the time of application

Journalists: confirmation that the sabbatical is focussed on the individual's learning and long-term development as a science journalist and acknowledgment that they should not report from their host institution during their residency
Curriculum vitae in English including permanent residential address, email and mobile phone contact
Samples of previous journalism work, which may be in any language, and which meet the requirements under Eligibility

All completed applications are checked for compliance with the selection criteria at the EMBO Office; applications proposing short-term placements for the purpose of content production will be rejected at this stage
documents: Proposal in English, maximum three pages
Curriculum vitae in English including permanent residential address, email and mobile phone number
Samples of previous journalism work in any language
Journalists only: confirmation that the sabbatical is focused on their learning and long-term development and that they will not report from the host institution during the residency
Researchers only: confirmation within the proposal that the placement will be a full-time internship or similar in a mainstream media newsroom producing published or broadcast science journalism
selection_criteria: All completed applications are acknowledged by email and checked at the EMBO Office for compliance with the selection criteria; applications proposing short-term placements for the purpose of content production are rejected at this stage
All completed and valid applications are reviewed by at least two members of the Advisory Board against the selection criteria
Ranked by the quality, ambition, intended goals and feasibility of the proposal
Ranked by the journalistic quality of the submitted work samples

In case of significant differences in the evaluation, an additional board member's opinion is sought; scholarships are awarded according to the ranking and the funding available for the scheme at the time, and the ranking and decisions of EMBO are not subject to review
coverage: Living expenses, via the daily subsistence stipend sized to the cost of living in the placement country
Travel costs connected with the placement, covered by the stipend and the published travel allowance
Travel and accommodation for the two-day EMBO Heidelberg workshop for Journalist Fellows
Fellows remain responsible for their own social security contributions, taxes and other costs incurred
application_method: Applications will only be accepted via the EMBO application portal, and only fully completed applications will be considered
Successful applicants must organize their own placements; EMBO provides written confirmation of a conditional offer subject to final confirmation from the relevant host institution / newsroom
official.application_route: Apply online through the EMBO application portal only (registration link on the programme page); fully completed applications must be registered by 23:59 CEST on 30 October, with selection once a year.
official.study_mode: Full-time, in-person placement; Fellows are expected not to undertake other work during the fellowship
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must reside in an EMBC Member State and their placement/s must also occur in an EMBC Member State; no citizenship criterion is published.
official.international_eligibility: Eligibility is residency-based rather than nationality-based: applicants must reside in an EMBC Member State and the placement must take place there, so the scheme cannot be used from or to outside EMBC Member States.
official.duration: Journalists: minimum three months, maximum six months. Researchers wishing to become science journalists: minimum three months, maximum 12 months, with periods longer than three months subject to an ongoing assessment process. It is not possible to extend the scholarship period.
official.description: EMBO describes the scheme as supporting science journalism by providing journalists with funded placements (sabbaticals) at one or more research institutions to deepen and broaden their knowledge of the life and associated sciences, and researchers wishing to transition full time to science journalism with funded placements in one or more media newsrooms so they can learn and train in journalism and develop a portfolio of work. Successful applicants receive a daily stipend based on the cost of living in the country of their placement/s, intended to cover living expenses and travel costs. The scheme was made possible by a private donation from Professor Maria Leptin.
official.region: EMBC Member States (Europe and associated countries); both the applicant's residence and the placement must be in an EMBC Member State
official.english_requirement: The proposal and curriculum vitae must be in English; samples of previous journalism work may be in any language.

not_confirmed: funding_amount: EMBO publishes the stipend only as per-country daily rates in Euro (EUR 68-140 per day, plus a travel allowance of mostly EUR 350), so there is no single figure to record
tuition_coverage wording: the scheme publishes no tuition component at all, as it funds placements rather than enrolled study
number of fellowships awarded per cycle: awards follow the Advisory Board ranking and the funding available for the scheme at the time
a cycle label such as '2026/2027': the pages state only that selection takes place once a year with applications accepted at any time
verification.notes: Stipend wording and coverage verified on EMBO's own Benefits page, with the actual amounts read from the subsistence-rates PDF hosted on embo.org and linked from that page; deadline, eligibility, application, selection and code-of-conduct details cross-checked across all official programme subpages on 2026-10-10.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a stipend-only fellowship, not a scholarship: EMBO pays a daily rate keyed to the cost of living in your placement country (EUR 68-140 per day from its published rates table) plus travel costs, for an in-person sabbatical of 3-6 months inside a research institution (3-12 months for scientists moving into a newsroom). You arrange the host yourself and the award stays conditional until that host confirms, so the proposal and the host negotiation are done before you apply. There is one deadline a year - a fully completed application registered by 23:59 CEST on 30 October - and a single award round with results by mid-November, so timing is everything. Because it is not tuition funding, budget for your own social security, taxes and any living costs above the subsistence rate.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Employed or freelance science journalists based in an EMBC Member State who want a funded, learning-focused sabbatical inside a life-science research institution, and mid-career life scientists with a master's or doctorate who already report on science and want to go full-time in a mainstream newsroom.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm early that you reside in an EMBC Member State and that your intended host institution or newsroom is also in an EMBC Member State, with an in-person placement
Contact and brief your proposed host before applying: EMBO expects the proposal to have been discussed with the host, even though written acceptance is not required at submission
Draft the proposal in English to a strict three-page maximum, naming the institution/newsroom and setting out concrete learning and knowledge outcomes
Select work samples that prove life-science journalism (published or broadcast); blog posts, social media and academic review articles do not count

Prepare an English CV that includes your permanent residential address, email and mobile phone number, and for journalists a statement that the sabbatical is learning-focused and will not produce reporting from the host institution
Register in the EMBO application portal well before 30 October and submit only when the application is complete, since incomplete applications are not considered
common_rejection_risks: Proposals that read as short-term placements for content production are rejected at the EMBO Office compliance check, before any Advisory Board review
Using AI tools to create the application is expressly forbidden by the programme's code of conduct and applicants are solely responsible for their content
Offering blog posts, social media output, or journal commentary/review articles as evidence of prior journalism - these are explicitly insufficient
Framing the fellowship around immediate publication opportunities rather than personal learning fails the Advisory Board's 'genuine desire' test
Virtual placements, placements outside EMBC Member States, or reporting on the host institution during the fellowship make an otherwise strong application ineligible
Incomplete portal submissions are not considered at all, and the selection decisions are not subject to review
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Everything beyond the daily subsistence stipend and the travel allowance: your own social security contributions, taxes and other costs incurred, any living costs above the country rate, relocation between placements, and income for the months between the mid-November decision and the start of the placement.
document_audit: The proposal must be in English and no more than three pages - treat the limit as a compliance boundary, not a guideline
The CV must be in English and must carry your permanent residential address, email and mobile phone number
Journalists must include the confirmation that the sabbatical is focused on their own learning and long-term development and that they will not report from the host institution during the residency

Researchers must spell out that the placement is a full-time internship or similar in a mainstream media newsroom producing published or broadcast science journalism, and attach prior life-science reporting evidence
Samples may be in any language, but each sample should be verifiable published or broadcast journalism with dates and outlets - reviewers rank them on journalistic quality
Successful applicants organise their own placements, so keep the host correspondence that shows you discussed the proposal with the institution/newsroom
alerts: One hard deadline a year: only fully completed applications registered in the EMBO portal by 23:59 CEST on 30 October are considered; a later submission simply waits for the next annual round
The scholarship period cannot be extended, so size the placement correctly from the start (3-6 months for journalists; 3-12 months for researchers, with reassessment beyond three months)
Fellows may not undertake other work during the fellowship, so the stipend is your whole income for that period
The offer is conditional on final confirmation by the host institution/newsroom - secure that confirmation immediately after selection or the cycle is lost
Multiple placements are allowed, but at least one must be in a different EMBC Member State than the other/s
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register and complete the application in the EMBO portal by 30 October; EMBO acknowledges by email and screens for compliance, then at least two Advisory Board members score and rank valid applications, and awards are made in ranking order against available funding.
